name: python-reference-lens
description: Shows Python references, calls, test/production counts, implementations and incoming call hierarchy above functions and methods.

pythonReferenceLens.enabled.description: Show reference CodeLens entries above Python functions and methods.

pythonReferenceLens.showZeroReferences.description: Show CodeLens entries with zero results, including calls, other references, implementations and callers.

pythonReferenceLens.showCalls.description: Show separate call-site and other-reference counts using the language provider's incoming call hierarchy.

pythonReferenceLens.showReferenceBreakdo.description: Show production and test counts in the total references lens.

pythonReferenceLens.testFilePatterns.description: Case-sensitive glob patterns identifying test files. Match paths relative to each caller's workspace folder (absolute paths outside the workspace), using forward slashes. Nonmatching files count as production.

pythonReferenceLens.showImplementations.description: Show implementations and overrides reported by the language provider.

pythonReferenceLens.showIncomingCalls.description: Show the number of distinct callers with a link to VS Code's incoming call hierarchy.

enumDescriptions: Use the original theme and restore colors previously changed by this extension.
Accent the border and title while keeping the theme's code and list backgrounds.
Use distinct backgrounds, a visible border and stronger selection highlights.
Start from Contrast and override individual colors with Peek Colors.
pythonReferenceLens.peekStyle.markdownDescription: Style the native reference/code popup. Adapts to light, dark and high-contrast themes. Requires an open folder/workspace. Writes theme-specific `workbench.colorCustomizations` at workspace scope, affecting **all native Peek views in this window**, including other languages. Choose `theme` to restore previous colors.

pythonReferenceLens.peekColors.markdownDescription: Color overrides when `#pythonReferenceLens.peekStyle#` is `custom`. Unspecified colors use the Contrast preset for the current theme. Use hex colors; a translucent value such as `#FFD43B33` is recommended for matchBackground. Code syntax colors remain controlled by the editor theme.

editorBackground.description: Code preview and line number gutter background.

matchBackground.description: Match highlighting in code and results. Prefer a translucent hex color.
